summary.text: Dark matter is an invisible form of matter that does not interact with light, and it is thought to act as the gravitational scaffolding for cosmic structures.
Its presence is implied by gravitational effects in galaxies, galaxy clusters and gravitational lensing that cannot be explained unless more matter exists than we can observe.
Fritz Zwicky found evidence of unseen mass in the Coma Cluster in 1933, and the idea took root in the 1970s.

facts.label: Zwicky's cluster
facts.value: The Coma Cluster, estimated at 400 times its visible mass

facts.label: Term in 1906
facts.value: Henri Poincaré used the term in 1906

facts.label: Local amount
facts.value: Out to Neptune, about the mass of a large asteroid

facts.label: Main candidates
facts.value: WIMPs, axions or primordial black holes

items.prompt: Zwicky weighed a galaxy cluster in two ways: by how its galaxies move, and by how much light it gives off. What did the two numbers show?

options.label: They agreed closely
The light-based figure was far larger
The motion-based figure was far larger
Neither could be worked out

items.explain: He compared a mass estimate from galaxy motions with one from brightness and number of galaxies, and found about 400 times more mass than was visible.

items.prompt: Zwicky's own picture of dark matter differs from today's. How did he think of it?

options.label: As ordinary matter that gives off no light
As an exotic particle never yet seen
As a form of energy that pushes outward
As a change to the laws of gravity

items.explain: Unlike modern theories, Zwicky considered dark matter to be non-luminous ordinary matter.

items.prompt: Why can scientists not just look for dark matter with a bigger telescope?

options.label: Current telescopes are simply not big enough yet
It does not interact with electromagnetic radiation, including light
It is hidden behind the brightest stars
It sits too far from Earth for a telescope to catch

items.explain: Dark matter does not interact with electromagnetic radiation, including light, so it is invisible and only its gravity shows.

items.prompt: Early dark matter work often guessed that unseen matter would be less than visible matter. How did that turn out?

options.label: It was confirmed by later work
It was later found to be false
It was never tested
It was true for galaxies only

items.explain: Poincaré concluded that dark matter would need to be less than visible matter, which was later found to be false.

items.prompt: A model has structures forming from the gradual build-up of slow-moving particles. Which kind of dark matter does it use?

options.label: Hot dark matter
Warm dark matter
Cold dark matter
Dark matter with no velocity at all

items.explain: Recent models favor a cold dark matter scenario, in which structures emerge by the gradual accumulation of particles.

items.prompt: How much of the universe's total mass, not counting energy, does dark matter make up?

options.label: About 85%
About 27%
About 5%
About 68%

items.explain: Dark matter constitutes 85% of the total mass; 26.8% is its share of the total mass-energy content.
